samples.summary: LoginPage's new provider-fetch wiring is never exercised: the stub returns `google: false`, which equals the component's initial state
samples.evidence: `page.tsx` adds `useEffect(() => fetchAuthProviders().then(p => setGoogleEnabled(p.google)))` and passes `googleEnabled` into `LoginForm`. The only LoginPage tests stub fetch with `{ github: true, google: false }` (login-form.test.tsx:117-125) and assert nothing about providers. Since `useState(false)` is the initial value, deleting the whole effect, mis-reading `providers.google`, or never passing the prop would leave both LoginPage tests green. The `googleEnabled=true` rendering is only tested by passing the prop directly to `LoginForm` (line 62), which bypasses the new page logic entirely. Net effect: a broken wiring ships as "Google button never appears" on every deployment that configured Google, with no failing test.

samples.summary: `fetchAuthProviders` has no direct test: the !res.ok fallback, the throw-to-fallback catch, and the `github !== false` / `google === true` coercion are all uncovered
samples.evidence: New exported function at api/auth.ts:130-165. `glob packages/frontend/src/api/**/*.test.*` lists analytics/ndjson/miro/share-image-url/documents/download-file/share-links/url tests — no auth.test.ts. Grep for `fetchAuthProviders` finds only page.tsx and a comment in login-form.test.tsx. So a regression that turned a network failure into a thrown rejection (breaking the login page) or that read a malformed body as `google: true` (showing a button that 404s) would go undetected.

samples.summary: Only one half of `emailIsVerified`'s two signals is covered — the `emails[0].verified === true` branch can be deleted with every test still passing
samples.evidence: google.strategy.ts:22-27 ORs `profile.emails?.[0]?.verified === true` with `profile._json?.email_verified === true`, and the comment claims either signal alone suffices. Every accepting fixture in the spec has `_json.email_verified: true` (makeProfile, line 36), including the "accepts the raw email_verified claim" test at line 86, which only proves the `_json` branch. There is no case with `emails: [{verified: true}]` and `_json.email_verified` false/absent, so removing the first disjunct is a surviving mutation; the resulting failure mode is verified users being refused sign-in.

samples.summary: `googleAuthPartiallyConfigured()`, `missingGoogleAuthVars()` and the AuthModule boot warning / conditional provider registration have no tests
samples.evidence: New exports in oauth-providers.ts and the `constructor()` warning plus `const googleProviders = googleAuthConfigured() ? [GoogleStrategy] : []` in auth.module.ts. Glob of packages/backend/src/auth/*.spec.ts shows no oauth-providers.spec.ts or auth.module.spec.ts; the only indirect coverage is `googleAuthConfigured` via auth.controller.spec's `GET /auth/providers` test and google-auth.guard.spec. A wrong missing-var list or an inverted partial check would silently mis-report the one diagnostic the optional provider offers.

samples.summary: No test asserts `GoogleCallbackGuard` does NOT mint a fresh state cookie when Google is configured
samples.evidence: google-auth.guard.ts documents the callback guard as "the same 404, without minting a new state", but the spec only exercises `GoogleCallbackGuard` in the unconfigured 404 case (line 81-87). Nothing asserts `cookie` is not called on a configured callback, so adding/keeping a `startWebOAuthLogin` call there — which would overwrite the state cookie mid-callback — would not fail any test.

samples.summary: The extracted `finishWebLogin` returnTo redirect is untested at controller level for either provider
samples.evidence: `finishWebLogin` reads the `loginReturn` cookie, clears it and redirects via `safeReturnPath` (auth.controller.ts:305-315). `grep returnTo|loginReturn` across packages/backend/**/*.spec.ts matches only google-auth.guard.spec.ts (the write side). auth.controller.spec's github and google success cases both use `cookies` without a return cookie and assert the plain frontend URL, so the refactor that moved this branch into a shared private method is covered only by `safeReturnPath` unit tests, not by any test that the controller still consults the cookie. A regression would silently drop template/deep-link returns after sign-in.
searchedFor: read auth.controller.spec.ts sections for github/google callbacks

samples.summary: The `photo` fallback to `_json.picture` is never exercised
samples.evidence: google.strategy.ts:93 uses `profile.photos?.[0]?.value ?? profile._json?.picture`; every spec fixture supplies `photos` (makeProfile line 26), so the fallback arm is dead in tests.

samples.summary: Google refusal cases assert no session cookie but never assert the state cookie was cleared on a failed match
samples.evidence: The GitHub-side comment and `consumeWebOAuthState` clear the state cookie whether or not it matches, so a failed login leaves nothing to replay. The google `refuses %s` table (auth.controller.spec.ts ~543-560) checks `res.redirect`, `res.cookie` not called and `findOrCreateUser` not called, but never `res.clearCookie` — so a regression that left the state cookie live after a refused callback would not be caught here.

verdict.reason: Verified in-repo. page.tsx:21-35,72 adds the provider-fetch effect and passes `googleEnabled` to LoginForm. The only LoginPage tests (login-form.test.tsx:117-125 stub, tests at 131-147) resolve `{github: true, google: false}` — identical to the `useState(false)` initial state — and assert only about the `?error=` alert, so deleting the effect, misreading `providers.google`, or omitting the prop all leave them green. The `googleEnabled=true` rendering is covered only by passing the prop directly to LoginForm (lines 62-69, 73-84), bypassing the page. I searched wide for a counterexample: repo-wide case-insensitive grep for LoginPage/login-page/"continue with google"/auth/providers finds no other test file; grep for `google: true` across packages/frontend/** returns zero test hits (only `startUrl("google")` at login-form.tsx:119); there is no e2e/playwright suite (`**/e2e/**` empty); `/login` hits in other tests are the CLI device-login and an unrelated Claude auth-smoke script; and there is no api/auth test file among the 242 frontend test files, so fetchAuthProviders' `body.google === true` mapping is untested too. Major under the test-adequacy rubric: a changed user-facing path (Google sign-in button visibility) with no test that can fail if the wiring breaks, shipping as "Google never appears" on deployments that configured it.
